items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Yes, and we had Adelle playing the harp.

ctx.x: Yes, and we had Adelle playing the harp. And people were paying to come and to listen. Now, you can imagine the shock that is to a musician who's always played on a stage for a stripper or an M.C. or a snake dancer, or some sort of act, which the band was to be heard but not seen, essentially.

And here, the whole thing is visual. You're up there being looked at and listened to. And no one's dancing. I just couldn't believe this was happening. And immediately, Joe says, come to work for me. And I said, but the union system -- I don't know if he used those words, 'fringe the union', but words to that effect. Come on, anyway.
